pinyin: shù nuó sǐ, rén nuó huó
literal: tree · move · dies, person · move · lives
natural: A tree dies when moved, a person thrives when moved

meaning.en: Changing environment is bad for a tree but good for a person; moving on may open new opportunities.
meaning.zh: 树换了地方容易死，人换个环境却可能有新的出路。

equivalents: A change is as good as a rest
Nothing ventured, nothing gained

examples.zh: 树挪死，人挪活，在这里干不下去，不如换个城市试试。
examples.en: If it isn't working here, try another city; a person moved can thrive.

examples.zh: 树挪死，人挪活，他辞职后反而做得风生水起。
examples.en: He quit and did better than ever.

usage.en: Used when advising someone to change job or place. Stresses opportunity in moving.
usage.zh: 常用来劝人换工作或换环境。

pinyin: shù gāo qiān zhàng, yè luò guī gēn
literal: tree · tall · thousand · zhang, leaf · fall · return · root
natural: However high the tree grows, its leaves fall back to the roots

meaning.en: No matter how far one goes, one eventually returns to one's native place.
meaning.zh: 无论走得多远，最终总要回到自己的故乡。

equivalents: There's no place like home
Home is where the heart is

examples.zh: 树高千丈，叶落归根，他退休后回了老家。
examples.en: However far one goes, one returns to the roots; after retirement he went back to his home town.

examples.zh: 海外华人常说树高千丈，叶落归根。
examples.en: Overseas Chinese often say that leaves fall back to the roots.

usage.en: Typically said of emigrants and old people returning to their native place.
usage.zh: 多指海外游子、老人终将回乡。

text: 水至清则无鱼，人至察则无徒
pinyin: shuǐ zhì qīng zé wú yú, rén zhì chá zé wú tú
literal: water · too · clear · then · no · fish, person · too · scrutinising · then · no · followers
natural: If water is too clear it has no fish; if you scrutinise people too closely you'll have no followers

meaning.en: Being too picky or exacting drives people away; be tolerant of small faults.
meaning.zh: 要求过于苛刻就没有人愿意追随，对小毛病应当宽容。

equivalents: Don't be too hard on people
Pick not holes in everything

examples.zh: 水至清则无鱼，人至察则无徒，当领导要有容人之量。
examples.en: Too-clear water has no fish and too-strict scrutiny no followers; a leader needs to be tolerant.

examples.zh: 水至清则无鱼，人至察则无徒，别对朋友太苛刻。
examples.en: Don't be too exacting with friends: too-clear water has no fish.

story.en: The line advises rulers that over-strict scrutiny leaves them without helpers.
story.zh: 《大戴礼记》中说“水至清则无鱼，人至察则无徒”，劝诫为官者不要过于苛察。

usage.en: Often shortened to 水至清则无鱼. Sometimes used to excuse sloppiness, so context matters.
usage.zh: 常简说“水至清则无鱼”，有时被用来为马虎找借口。

pinyin: wū lòu piān féng lián yè yǔ
literal: house · leaks · just · meets · successive · nights · rain
natural: The roof leaks, and it just so happens to rain night after night

meaning.en: Misfortunes come one after another; when things go wrong, they go wrong in a row.
meaning.zh: 倒霉的事接连发生，祸不单行。

equivalents: When it rains, it pours
Misfortunes never come singly

examples.zh: 刚丢了工作，孩子又生了病，真是屋漏偏逢连夜雨。
examples.en: He'd just lost his job when his child fell ill: when it rains it pours.

examples.zh: 屋漏偏逢连夜雨，车坏了，手机也没电了。
examples.en: The car broke down and then the phone died; misfortunes never come singly.

usage.en: Often paired with 船迟又遇打头风. Common in news and conversation.
usage.zh: 常与“船迟又遇打头风”对举。

pinyin: shě bù de hái zi tào bù zháo láng
literal: unwilling to part with · child · snare · not · catch · wolf
natural: If you can't bear to lose the child, you can't snare the wolf

meaning.en: You must be willing to pay a price to get something big.
meaning.zh: 想得到大的好处，就得舍得付出代价。

equivalents: Nothing ventured, nothing gained
You can't make an omelette without breaking eggs

examples.zh: 舍不得孩子套不着狼，想做大生意就得先投入。
examples.en: You can't snare a wolf without risking the child; to build a big business you have to invest first.

examples.zh: 舍不得孩子套不着狼，他卖掉房子开了公司。
examples.en: He sold his house to start a company; no gain without sacrifice.

usage.en: Originally the 孩子 is bait (often a child's shoe in folk telling). Used to encourage taking risks.
usage.zh: 常用来鼓励为大目标冒险投入。

pinyin: shě de shě de, yǒu shě cái yǒu dé
literal: give up · gain · give up · gain, have · giving · only then · have · gain
natural: To give is to gain; only by giving up can you get

meaning.en: You gain something only by being willing to give something up.
meaning.zh: 有所付出才有收获，舍弃是得到的前提。

equivalents: Nothing ventured, nothing gained
You have to give to get

examples.zh: 舍得舍得，有舍才有得，想进步就要舍得花时间学习。
examples.en: To give is to gain; to improve you must be willing to spend time studying.

examples.zh: 舍得舍得，有舍才有得，他放弃高薪去创业。
examples.en: He gave up a high salary to start a business, believing that only giving up brings gain.

usage.en: The pun 舍得 (shědé, 'be willing to give up') / 舍/得 (give / gain) is the point of the saying.
usage.zh: 此语巧用“舍得”一词拆开解释：舍与得。

pinyin: yī bù cuò, bù bù cuò
literal: one · step · wrong, step · step · wrong
natural: One wrong step, wrong at every step

meaning.en: One early mistake leads to a series of further errors.
meaning.zh: 一步走错，后面就会接连出错。

equivalents: One false step leads to another
A bad beginning makes a bad ending

examples.zh: 下棋最怕一步错，步步错。
examples.en: In chess the worst thing is one wrong move leading to the next.

examples.zh: 一步错，步步错，他后悔当初没听劝。
examples.en: One wrong step, wrong at every step; he regrets not taking advice.

usage.en: Common in chess talk and life advice. Often shortened: 一步错，满盘皆输 is related.
usage.zh: 常用于下棋和人生告诫。

pinyin: yī kǒu tuò mò yī gè dīng
literal: one · mouthful · spit · one · nail
natural: Every spit is a nail

meaning.en: What I say, I will do; my word is binding.
meaning.zh: 说话算数，说出的话就像钉进木头的钉子，不能反悔。

equivalents: My word is my bond
A man's word is his bond

examples.zh: 我一口唾沫一个钉，答应你的事一定办到。
examples.en: My word is my bond; I'll do what I promised.

examples.zh: 他向来一口唾沫一个钉，从不食言。
examples.en: His word is his bond; he never goes back on it.

usage.en: A somewhat rustic, emphatic way of promising. 唾沫 is pronounced tuò mo.
usage.zh: 带乡土味的强调说法，唾沫读作 tuò mo。

pinyin: yī dòng bù rú yī jìng
literal: one · move · not · as good as · one · stay still
natural: Staying still beats moving

meaning.en: It's better to leave things as they are than to make changes.
meaning.zh: 与其折腾，不如保持现状。

equivalents: Let sleeping dogs lie
If it ain't broke, don't fix it

examples.zh: 系统运行得好好的，一动不如一静，先别升级了。
examples.en: The system runs fine, so better to stay put than to touch it; don't upgrade yet.

examples.zh: 他觉得一动不如一静，所以一直没换工作。
examples.en: He thinks it's better to stay still, so he never changed jobs.

usage.en: Can sound conservative or cautious depending on tone. Opposite of 树挪死，人挪活 in spirit.
usage.zh: 带保守谨慎的意味，与“树挪死，人挪活”相对。

pinyin: yī shì bù fán èr zhǔ
literal: one · matter · not · trouble · two · masters
natural: One matter shouldn't trouble two hosts

meaning.en: If someone has started a job for you, ask the same person to finish it rather than another.
meaning.zh: 一件事情已经麻烦了一个人，就不再去麻烦第二个人。

equivalents: Don't change horses in midstream

examples.zh: 既然你已经开了头，一事不烦二主，后面的事也拜托你吧。
examples.en: Since you've started it, let's not trouble a second person; please finish the rest too.

examples.zh: 一事不烦二主，这批货就一起交给你办吧。
examples.en: One matter shouldn't trouble two people; I'll hand this shipment to you too.

usage.en: Polite, used when asking a helpful person to take on more.
usage.zh: 客气话，请已经帮忙的人继续把事办完。

pinyin: yī huí shēng, èr huí shú
literal: first · time · strange, second · time · familiar
natural: First time strange, second time familiar

meaning.en: Things that feel unfamiliar the first time become easy with repetition.
meaning.zh: 第一次接触觉得陌生，多接触几次就熟悉了。

equivalents: Practice makes perfect
Familiarity breeds comfort

examples.zh: 一回生，二回熟，多练几次就不紧张了。
examples.en: First time strange, second time familiar; after a few tries you won't be nervous.

examples.zh: 别怕，一回生，二回熟。
examples.en: Don't be afraid: the first time is the hardest.

usage.en: Said to encourage beginners and to put strangers at ease.
usage.zh: 常用于鼓励新手，或让陌生人放松。

text: 不要把鸡蛋放在同一个篮子里
pinyin: bù yào bǎ jī dàn fàng zài tóng yī gè lán zi lǐ
literal: not · should · put · eggs · in · same · one · basket · inside
natural: Don't put all your eggs in one basket

meaning.en: Spread your risk instead of staking everything on one thing.
meaning.zh: 要分散风险，不要把全部赌注押在同一件事上。

equivalents: Don't put all your eggs in one basket

examples.zh: 理财时不要把鸡蛋放在同一个篮子里。
examples.en: When investing, don't put all your eggs in one basket.

examples.zh: 不要把鸡蛋放在同一个篮子里，你最好多找几家供应商。
examples.en: Don't put all your eggs in one basket; you'd better line up several suppliers.

usage.en: A calque of the English proverb, now fully established in Chinese, especially in finance and business.
usage.zh: 译自英语谚语，在理财和商业中尤为常用。

pinyin: xiǎo dòng bù bǔ, dà dòng chī kǔ
literal: small · hole · not · mend, big · hole · suffer
natural: Mend a small hole now or suffer from a big one later

meaning.en: Fix small problems early or they grow into big troubles.
meaning.zh: 小问题不及时处理，将来就会酿成大麻烦。

equivalents: A stitch in time saves nine

examples.zh: 小洞不补，大洞吃苦，屋顶漏水要及时修。
examples.en: Fix small holes before they become big ones; repair a leaking roof promptly.

examples.zh: 小洞不补，大洞吃苦，账目上的小错误也要马上改。
examples.en: Even small errors in the accounts should be corrected at once.

usage.en: Common in management and safety advice.
usage.zh: 常用于管理、安全等方面的告诫。

pinyin: xiǎo xīn shǐ de wàn nián chuán
literal: careful · sail · can · ten thousand · year · boat
natural: Careful sailing keeps a boat afloat for ten thousand years

meaning.en: Being cautious keeps you safe in the long run.
meaning.zh: 谨慎行事才能长久平安。

equivalents: Better safe than sorry
Discretion is the better part of valour

examples.zh: 小心驶得万年船，出门前再检查一遍门窗。
examples.en: Careful sailing lasts long; check the doors and windows once more before going out.

examples.zh: 小心驶得万年船，投资还是稳妥点好。
examples.en: Better safe than sorry; it's best to invest cautiously.

usage.en: The 'sailing' image: 驶 means to sail or drive. Used to counsel caution.
usage.zh: “驶”指行船、开车。用于劝人谨慎。

text: 天不生无禄之人，地不长无名之草
pinyin: tiān bù shēng wú lù zhī rén, dì bù zhǎng wú míng zhī cǎo
literal: heaven · not · bear · without · livelihood · person, earth · not · grow · without · name · grass
natural: Heaven doesn't create people without a livelihood, nor earth plants without a name

meaning.en: Everyone has a way to make a living and a place in the world.
meaning.zh: 每个人都有谋生的出路和存在的价值。

equivalents: God never shuts one door but he opens another
Where there's a will, there's a way

examples.zh: 天不生无禄之人，地不长无名之草，你不用太担心前途。
examples.en: Heaven makes no one without a livelihood; don't worry too much about your future.

examples.zh: 天不生无禄之人，地不长无名之草，总会有出路的。
examples.en: Every person has a way to make a living; something will turn up.

usage.en: Often an encouragement to the jobless or disheartened.
usage.zh: 常用来安慰失业或灰心的人。

pinyin: tiān shàng bù huì diào xiàn bǐng
literal: sky · above · not · will · drop · filled pie
natural: Pies don't fall from the sky

meaning.en: There is no such thing as a free lunch; be wary of too-good-to-be-true offers.
meaning.zh: 不会有不劳而获的好事，要警惕天上掉馅饼式的诱惑。

equivalents: There's no such thing as a free lunch
If it sounds too good to be true, it probably is

examples.zh: 天上不会掉馅饼，高额回报的投资多半是骗局。
examples.en: There's no free lunch; high-return investments are mostly scams.

examples.zh: 天上不会掉馅饼，别轻信陌生人的好事。
examples.en: Pies don't fall from the sky, so don't trust strangers offering great deals.

usage.en: Very common in anti-fraud warnings, together with 天上掉馅饼 (windfall).
usage.zh: 在反诈宣传中很常见。

pinyin: tiān yào xià yǔ, niáng yào jià rén
literal: sky · will · rain, mother · will · remarry
natural: Rain will fall and Mother will remarry

meaning.en: Some things are inevitable and nobody can stop them.
meaning.zh: 有些事情不可避免，谁也拦不住。

equivalents: What will be, will be
You can't stop the rain

examples.zh: 天要下雨，娘要嫁人，他想走就让他走吧。
examples.en: Rain will fall, a widow will remarry; if he wants to leave, let him go.

examples.zh: 天要下雨，娘要嫁人，随他去吧。
examples.en: Rain falls and mothers remarry; let it be.

usage.en: Often said with a shrug of resignation; the next line in the full saying is 由她去. 娘 here means mother.
usage.zh: 常带无奈口吻。

pinyin: tiān jī bù kě xiè lòu
literal: heaven's · secret · not · may · be leaked
natural: Heaven's secrets must not be revealed

meaning.en: Some secrets must stay secret; also used jokingly to refuse to disclose something.
meaning.zh: 天意或机密不能泄露；今多用于调侃，表示不肯透露。

equivalents: That's a secret
My lips are sealed

examples.zh: 你问我结果？天机不可泄露。
examples.en: You ask me the result? Heaven's secrets must not be revealed.

examples.zh: 天机不可泄露，到时候你就知道了。
examples.en: It's a secret; you'll find out when the time comes.

usage.en: Originally said by fortune-tellers; now often playful, e.g. to keep a surprise.
usage.zh: 原为算命先生的话，今多半开玩笑，用来保密。

pinyin: hǔ luò píng yáng bèi quǎn qī
literal: tiger · falls to · flat plains · by · dogs · bullied
natural: A tiger on the plains is bullied by dogs

meaning.en: A powerful person who has lost their position is mocked by inferiors.
meaning.zh: 有权势的人一旦失势，就会被小人欺负。

equivalents: A lion in a cage is baited by mice
Fallen greatness is mocked by small men

examples.zh: 他下台后门庭冷落，真是虎落平阳被犬欺。
examples.en: After he left office nobody visited; a tiger on the plains is bullied by dogs.

examples.zh: 虎落平阳被犬欺，当年的老部下现在对他爱理不理。
examples.en: A fallen tiger is bullied by dogs; his former subordinates now ignore him.

usage.en: Often paired with 龙游浅水遭虾戏. Used to sympathise with someone who has lost status.
usage.zh: 常与“龙游浅水遭虾戏”对举，表示同情失势的人。

pinyin: lóng yóu qiǎn shuǐ zāo xiā xì
literal: dragon · swims · shallow · water · suffers · shrimp · teasing
natural: A dragon in shallow water is teased by shrimps

meaning.en: Talented people in a bad situation are bullied by worthless ones.
meaning.zh: 有才能的人处境不利时，被庸人戏弄。

equivalents: A lion in a cage is baited by mice

examples.zh: 龙游浅水遭虾戏，有才的人被排挤也很常见。
examples.en: A dragon in shallows is teased by shrimps; talented people are often squeezed out.

examples.zh: 龙游浅水遭虾戏，他只好忍气吞声。
examples.en: A dragon in shallow water is teased by shrimp; he could only swallow his anger.

usage.en: Usually quoted with 虎落平阳被犬欺 as a pair.
usage.zh: 常与“虎落平阳被犬欺”并用。

pinyin: yú yǔ xióng zhǎng bù kě jiān dé
literal: fish · and · bear's paw · not · can · both · get
natural: You can't have both fish and bear's paw

meaning.en: You can't have two desirable things at once; you must choose.
meaning.zh: 两样都想要的东西不能同时得到，只能取舍。

equivalents: You can't have your cake and eat it
You can't have it both ways

examples.zh: 工作和家庭常常是鱼与熊掌不可兼得。
examples.en: Work and family are often a case of not being able to have both.

examples.zh: 鱼与熊掌不可兼得，你得在两份工作邀请中选一个。
examples.en: You can't have both fish and bear's paw; you must choose one of the two offers.

story.en: Mencius says that if he can't have both fish and bear's paw he will choose the paw, as he would choose righteousness over life.
story.zh: 孟子说：“鱼，我所欲也；熊掌，亦我所欲也；二者不可得兼，舍鱼而取熊掌者也。”

usage.en: Adapted from Mencius's passage on choosing righteousness over life.
usage.zh: 化用《孟子》“鱼，我所欲也；熊掌，亦我所欲也；二者不可得兼”。

synonyms: 鱼，我所欲也，熊掌亦我所欲也

text: 鱼找鱼，虾找虾，乌龟专找王八
pinyin: yú zhǎo yú, xiā zhǎo xiā, wū guī zhuān zhǎo wáng bā
literal: fish · seek · fish, shrimp · seek · shrimp, tortoise · specially · seek · turtle
natural: Fish seek fish, shrimp seek shrimp, and tortoises seek turtles

meaning.en: People tend to associate with their own kind.
meaning.zh: 人总是和自己同类的人交往。

equivalents: Birds of a feather flock together

examples.zh: 鱼找鱼，虾找虾，乌龟专找王八，他的朋友都是一路货色。
examples.en: Fish seek fish, shrimp seek shrimp; his friends are all cut from the same cloth.

examples.zh: 鱼找鱼，虾找虾，乌龟专找王八，物以类聚嘛。
examples.en: Birds of a feather flock together.

usage.en: Casual and slightly rude (王八 is an insult); used jokingly or disparagingly.
usage.zh: 口语，略带粗俗，含调侃或贬义。

variants: 鱼找鱼，虾找虾，乌龟爱王八——气味相投

pinyin: jī dàn lǐ tiāo gǔ tou
literal: egg · inside · pick · bone
natural: Pick bones out of an egg

meaning.en: To find fault with something that has no faults; to nitpick.
meaning.zh: 在没有毛病的地方硬找毛病。

equivalents: To pick holes
To split hairs
To nitpick

examples.zh: 他这个人爱鸡蛋里挑骨头，怎么做都不满意。
examples.en: He loves nitpicking and is never satisfied no matter what you do.

examples.zh: 你这是鸡蛋里挑骨头，方案明明已经很完善了。
examples.en: You're picking bones from an egg; the plan is already thorough.

usage.en: Usually a verb phrase: 在……上鸡蛋里挑骨头. Casual, critical.
usage.zh: 常作谓语。口语，带批评意味。

pinyin: nìng wéi jī tóu, bù wéi fèng wěi
literal: rather · be · chicken · head, not · be · phoenix · tail
natural: Better to be a chicken's head than a phoenix's tail

meaning.en: Better to lead in a small group than to follow in a large, prestigious one.
meaning.zh: 宁愿在小地方当头儿，也不愿在大地方做跟随者。

equivalents: Better to reign in hell than serve in heaven
Better be the head of a dog than the tail of a lion

examples.zh: 宁为鸡头，不为凤尾，他选择了一家小公司当负责人。
examples.en: Better to be a chicken's head than a phoenix's tail; he chose to head a small company.

examples.zh: 宁为鸡头，不为凤尾，可是大平台的机会也不能错过。
examples.en: Better the head of a chicken than the tail of a phoenix, but don't miss big-platform chances either.

usage.en: Often debated against the opposite advice 宁为凤尾，不为鸡头.
usage.zh: 常与相反的说法“宁为凤尾，不为鸡头”对比讨论。
